facts.fact_text: According to the incident report drawn up on 17 October 2003, fifty to sixty persons, including the applicants, gathered in a square in Istanbul at 7.45 p.m.
According to the incident report drawn up on 17 October 2003, the persons gathered in the square in Istanbul chanted anti-war slogans.

According to the incident report drawn up on 17 October 2003, the persons gathered in the square were protesting against the Government's proposals to send soldiers to participate in the invasion of Iraq.
According to the incident report drawn up on 17 October 2003, a total of six persons, including the applicants, were arrested and taken to a police station at 8.30 p.m. on 17 October 2003.
The applicants remained in police custody until their release the day following their arrest on 17 October 2003, i.e. on 18 October 2003.

On 21 October 2003 criminal proceedings were instigated against the applicants for having taken part in an unlawful demonstration, in breach of sections 33, 36 and 40 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).

According to the incident report drawn up on 17 October 2003, the police warned the gathered persons using loudspeakers that they were disturbing the flow of traffic.
According to the incident report drawn up on 17 October 2003, the police asked the gathered persons to disperse but were unsuccessful.
According to the incident report drawn up on 17 October 2003, the police had to use force against a number of the demonstrators who displayed rowdy behaviour.

In deciding to close the investigation on 14 April 2004, the Bakırköy prosecutor considered, on the basis of the documents in the file, that when the applicants refused to disperse the police had had to use force against them.

According to the incident report drawn up on 17 October 2003, when the police attempted to arrest some of the demonstrators and put them into police vehicles, a number of the demonstrators displayed rowdy behaviour.
According to the incident report drawn up on 17 October 2003, the police had to use force against a number of the demonstrators who displayed rowdy behaviour.
The Bakırköy prosecutor concluded that the applicants' simple injuries had been caused when the police were exercising their statutory powers on the use of force.
The Bakırköy Criminal Court of First Instance held, in its judgment of 28 January 2008, that the applicants had exercised their democratic rights and had not committed any offences.
The applicants allege that they were subjected to ill-treatment during their arrest on 17 October 2003.
The applicants allege that they were subjected to ill-treatment during their detention in police custody following their arrest on 17 October 2003.
The fourth applicant complained to the Bakırköy prosecutor that he had been beaten up by police officers.
The first applicant complained to the Bakırköy prosecutor that police chief M. T. had sworn at him/her during his/her time in police custody.
The fourth applicant complained to the Bakırköy prosecutor that police chief M. T. had sworn at him during his time in police custody.
On 21 October 2003 the Bakırköy prosecutor asked for an investigation to be opened into the applicants' allegations of ill-treatment.
On 14 April 2004 the Bakırköy prosecutor decided to close the investigation into the applicants' allegations of ill-treatment.
